title: Reuse order of call temporaries across statements: SIO_$INIT and TIME_$SET_ITIMER reuse the last-allocated slot first (LIFO), dpc restarts each call at the frame base
description: codegen-patterns 1.5 'Expression by address' / lower.rs assign_temps: dpc gives each call's temporaries offsets from the frame base down, in push order. The image's later calls take the most recently allocated slot first. SIO_$INIT 0xE32C28..0xE32E04 (tools/pcsurvey.py temps): call 1 temps -8 then -12 (push order); the next one-temp call -12 (E32C98, dpc: -8); then -12,-8 (E32CCC/E32CDE: push order reversed against dpc's -8,-12); then -8,-12; then -12; then -12,-8. Consistent with a free list used as a stack, a statement's temporaries freed in allocation order. TIME_$SET_ITIMER 0xE58E58: statement 1 has two hidden-result temporaries -8, -0x10 (pea at 0xE58EA8, 0xE58EB8); statements 2 and 3 (single calls) take -0x10 (pea at 0xE58ED4, 0xE58EEA), dpc -8. description: Branch threading (o6p) sends the outer back edge to the inner while's test; the outer head then falls into the while's opening bra and is no longer a branch target. Compiled code has no 0x2048 filler before a fall-through bra (loopalign fillers: only ASKNODE_$INTERNET_INFO 0xE649E6, a jump-table label per codegen-patterns 7), and no such head is seen in aligning code: whether the original aligns it is unknown. dpc refuses (thread_branches). description: Found in bead hs92. dpc (main and hs92) schedules `clr.l -(SP); movea.l #QUIT_EC,A0; move.l (CLOCKH).l,-(SP); move.w (AS_ID).l,D0; lsl.w ...; pea (0,A0,D0.w)` for an element of another unit's array pushed after two other arguments (by address or addr() by value). The image pushes the element off the register holding hdr's slot, `pea (-0x1,A2,D3*1)' (0xE12478 in PKT_$BRK_INTERNET_HDR 0xE12328; 0xE12300 in PKT_$BLD_INTERNET_HDR 0xE1202C): the transfer and dereference fold to the parameter's own address.  dpc's IR lowers Deref(Transfer(AddrOf(x))) to Addr::Indirect on Expr::AddrOf and the selector refuses ("this pointer expression is not supported yet" / "passing this kind of object by address"), for any x (var/in parameter, local).  Both routines are blocked earlier too (run-time min, packed field).  Settle whether T(addr(x))^ folds to x's address when T's target is not x's type (p. 4-197 transfer; the element's indexing then uses T's array bounds) and implement.

Only srcsurvey mismatch in KBD_$PUT and KBD_$SET_KBD_TYPE, first difference in TTY_$I_SET_RAW, a component of TTY_$K_ENABLE_FUNC (with bks D0-park). Shape: status out-param address loaded at entry and pushed (pea), then p := f(..., status) kept in an address register: image puts the param in A3 and the call result in A2 (enable_func: params at (12,A6)->A3, (20,A6)->A2, the result parked in D0 then movea.l D0,A2). codegen-patterns 12.4 R1a (allocation order not settled; dpc: address order of first definition). title: Calls of an abnormal routine (FIM_$CLEANUP): no register holds a value across them (23 of 23 compiled callers); dpc does not model it, MAC_$SEND refused
description: Found with bead domain-pascal-ei42 (codegen-patterns 9, 'abnormal'). In all 23 compiled routines that call FIM_$CLEANUP 0xE21634 only its D0 result is live across the call (other calls of the same routines do have held values: MAC_OS_$SEND A4 across 0xE0B750). Parameters needed after it are re-read from their slots (MAC_$SEND 0xE0BB12: (0x14) in A1 at 0xE0BB26 for the statements before the call, then movea.l (0x14,A6),A1 at 0xE0BBB2, 0xE0BC2A, 0xE0BC3E), a with element address is stored to a frame slot (0xE0BB44, read at 0xE0BB9E). dpc keeps entry-loaded parameters in registers across it: MAC_$SEND fails with 'more values live at once than there are registers'. Needs: the IR to mark calls of abnormal routines (ref 5.5.6 p. 5-19), entry loads cut at such a call and the parameter read from its slot after it; until then a specific refusal would be safer than the register-count one.

description: Found under domain-pascal-bdi0 (codegen-patterns 3, 'nil results').  In a body of several statements dpc holds a pointer result variable in an address register (set_pointer_result_web) and accepts it in A0 when no call follows.  Where every assignment of the result is last (nothing but the epilogue after it in the text), the image stores into the result slot and reloads at the join: SIO_$I_GET_DESC 0xE66808 'move.l (28,A0,D0.w),(-4,A6)' then 0xE6680E 'movea.l (-4,A6),A0' (the error path branches to the reload with the slot unwritten); KBD_$GET_DESC 0xE1AA92/0xE1AA98; TTY_$I_GET_DESC 0xE667B0/0xE667B6; NET_$FIND_HANDLER 0xE5A178/0xE5A180/0xE5A184 (nil 'clr.l (-0x10,A6)' too).  dpc gives 'movea.l mem,A0' for e.g. 'count := 0; if tab[k] = nil then count := 5 else f := tab[k]' (checked with main's dpc).  Where some assignment is not last (followed by return/goto/statements, or in a loop), the image does hold it in a register (14 nil sites, codegen-patterns 3).  bdi0 refuses nil in the all-last shape; the memory and call forms are unchanged (fixing them changes output: MISMATCH kbd_$get_desc in the srcsurvey baseline may be this).
